subject: Hosted API console copy: short privacy blurb & subprocessor transparency
messages:
From: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acme-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: data-privacy@acme-analytics.com
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Quick clarifications on Hosted API console privacy text

Hi Marissa —

Thanks for the walkthrough earlier. Our privacy and legal teams asked for two small updates before we include Redwood in our developer docs: 

1) A one-sentence plain-language summary in the console about what data Redwood stores from requests to the Hosted API and for how long (we need something short for the onboarding modal).
2) A clear link to the current subprocessor list and a statement about international transfers (we operate across US/EU).

Can you share proposed console copy and confirm whether the subprocessor list you send is the same one referenced in the DPA? If there are any recent changes to the list or differences between hosted/dedicated, please highlight.

Best,
Emma
Emma Sullivan
Privacy Counsel, Acme Analytics
[Acme logo]

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acme-analytics.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 14 Dec 2026 18:10:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on Hosted API console privacy text

Hi Emma —

Thanks for the clear asks. Drafting two short options below for the onboarding modal (25–40 words each). We can pick one and I’ll coordinate the linked docs. Also attaching the current subprocessor snapshot and a preliminary redline of the DPA highlighting transfer text.

Option A (very short):
“Redwood processes request data to generate responses. We retain request metadata and full content for up to 30 days to improve reliability and billing; content used for model improvement only with customer consent. See the subprocessor list and transfer details.”

Option B (privacy-forward):
"We temporarily store request content and metadata for up to 30 days to support reliability and billing. We never use your data to train models unless you opt in; see our subprocessor list and international transfer practices for details."

Notes: 
- The phrase “model improvement” vs “train models” is often flagged by customers — Kimberly, should we standardize to "train models"?
- Subprocessor list: attached PDF is the canonical hosted API list as of 2026-12-10. Dedicated/private deployments have a smaller set — Laura, can you confirm we should explicitly call that out in the modal?

Attachments: [subprocessors_list_202612.pdf] [dpa_redline_acme_202612.docx]

Thanks — happy to iterate.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Product Counsel, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com
+1 (415) 555-0123

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acme-analytics.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 08:07:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on Hosted API console privacy text

Marissa / Laura —

I prefer Option B but with one tweak for plain language: replace “we never use your data to train models unless you opt in” with “we do not use your data to train our models unless you explicitly opt in.” Small change, clearer to legal reviewers.

Laura — I agree we should call out differences between Hosted vs Dedicated/Private in the modal but keep it one sentence and link to a longer FAQ. Proposed line: 

"Hosted API requests may be processed by subprocessors across multiple regions; Dedicated and Private deployments use a limited subprocessor set under customer control — see the subprocessor map."

Also: per the DPA redline, Acme asked whether the subprocessor PDF is versioned and discoverable via a stable link (we currently publish a snapshot on the privacy portal). Emma — we can provide a stable URL and an archive of prior snapshots if that helps your audit trail.

K

—Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Senior Privacy Program Manager, Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
To: Emma Sullivan <emma.sullivan@acme-analytics.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 15 Dec 2026 11:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Quick clarifications on Hosted API console privacy text

Emma —

Thanks for the request and for reviewing the redline. Quick confirmations: 

- The attached subprocessors_list_202612.pdf is the canonical hosted API snapshot; we maintain a public, versioned list at the link below and will add an archive entry for the date you need for your compliance review.
- Dedicated/Private: the modal will say "Dedicated and Private customers can request the restricted subprocessor list in their deployment agreement" and link to the DPA redline.
- International transfers: for Hosted API we rely on standard contractual mechanisms and, where applicable, transfer frameworks; the console copy will link to the DPA section titled 'Cross-Border Transfers' for the full text.

Proposed final console copy (single 34-word sentence for the onboarding modal):

"We temporarily store request content and metadata for up to 30 days to support reliability and billing; we do not use your data to train our models unless you explicitly opt in — see our subprocessor list and transfer practices."

Action items: 
1) Marissa: please confirm placement in the onboarding modal and provide the stable link (I’ll add the version tag).
2) Kimberly: I’ll incorporate your one-line Hosted vs Dedicated distinction into the FAQ content.
3) Emma: I’ll upload the archived subprocessor snapshot for 2026-12-10 and add a signed statement that the PDF matches the DPA reference.

Links: https://drive.google.com/drive/folders/1a2b3cRedwood-Acme-Privacy

Laura Bennett
Director, Trust & Privacy, Redwood Inference
laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
